prompt: What does a private endpoint do to a service's public endpoint?

choices.text: Removes it automatically
choices.why: It stays until publicNetworkAccess is disabled.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. Closing the public path is a separate setting.

choices.text: Moves it behind Front Door
choices.why: Front Door is a separate service, unrelated to private endpoints.

choices.text: Restricts it to Azure subnets, like a service endpoint
choices.why: That is what a service endpoint does; a private endpoint adds a private address.

prompt: Match each way of reaching a service to what happens to its public endpoint.
hint: Only one adds a private address.

prompt: The endpoint exists and is approved, but an app in vnet-shop still reaches the SQL server's public address. Which resource is the likely gap?
hint: Who answers the name inside the network?

choices.text: The private endpoint's network interface
choices.why: It exists; the name just does not point at it.

choices.text: A second SQL server
choices.why: One server is enough; the issue is resolution.

choices.text: The zone's link to the network
choices.why: Right. Without it, nobody in the network uses the zone.

choices.text: An NSG rule allowing port 1433
choices.why: That is about traffic, not about which address the name returns.

prompt: Why does the zone's name use `environment().suffixes.sqlServerHostname`?
hint: Not every Azure cloud has the same suffix.

choices.text: So the same file works in other Azure clouds
choices.why: Right. Sovereign clouds use different domain suffixes.

choices.text: Zone names must be computed, never written
choices.why: A literal name works in the public cloud; the function is for portability.

choices.text: It hides the zone's name from the internet
choices.why: Private zones are not public anyway; the name is not secret.

choices.text: It makes the zone resolve public names too
choices.why: The zone answers only its own records.

prompt: For a private endpoint to a SQL server, `groupIds` holds the value ___.
The private endpoint works from Azure VMs but not from the office over VPN. What is the likely fix?
hint: Which DNS does the office ask?

choices.text: A second private endpoint for the office
choices.why: One endpoint serves both; the office cannot resolve it.

choices.text: Turning public network access back on
choices.why: That reopens the door the lesson closed.

choices.text: A larger VPN gateway
choices.why: Bandwidth is not the problem; the name is.

choices.text: A forwarder or DNS Private Resolver for privatelink domains
choices.why: Right. On-premises queries must reach Azure's resolver.

prompt: A connection to a private endpoint fails. What does the lesson test first?
hint: A DNS question until proven otherwise.

choices.text: The SQL password
choices.why: Authentication comes after the address is right.

choices.text: Resolve the name from where the client runs
choices.why: Right. Compare the answer with the endpoint's address.

choices.text: Restart the SQL server
choices.why: Nothing about a restart changes which address a name returns.

choices.text: Recreate the private endpoint in another subnet
choices.why: Before changing anything, find out what the name resolves to.

prompt: A custom DNS server in the network should forward to Azure's resolver at 168.63.129.___.
hint: The last part of the address.

prompt: Why does the shop assign a `deny` policy instead of only setting publicNetworkAccess to Disabled?
hint: Who will turn it back on?

choices.text: The property cannot be set in Bicep
choices.why: It can; lesson 17's vault does.

choices.text: So nobody quietly turns it back on
choices.why: Right. The policy refuses the change at Resource Manager.

choices.text: Policies are cheaper than private endpoints
choices.why: They do different jobs; cost is not the reason.

choices.text: A deny policy also creates the private endpoint
choices.why: It refuses; it creates nothing.

prompt: Put the shop's steps for closing the SQL server's public path in order.
items: Create the private endpoint, zone, link and zone group
Check the name resolves privately from the app's network
Set publicNetworkAccess to Disabled on existing servers
Assign the deny policy at the subscription
trap: Disabling public access before the private path resolves is the slip: the app loses its database.

prompt: Which of these are true after the lesson's files are deployed? Choose all that apply.
hint: Private path, one zone, one policy.

choices.text: The app's connection string does not change
choices.why: Yes. The same name answers privately.

choices.text: Existing public SQL servers are switched off by the policy
choices.why: No. Deny stops new violations; existing ones show as non-compliant.

choices.text: A new SQL server with public access is refused
choices.why: Yes. By Resource Manager, whatever tool sent it.

choices.text: The office resolves the private address with no further setup
choices.why: No. It needs a forwarder or the DNS Private Resolver.
